findings.text: the fast-cap --map and unset-cap exit checks pass whether or not the cap is applied, now that it never fails a run
a cancelled or failed earlier main run breaks the 3-in-a-row trend, even for a job that ran past the limit
the trend test holds no 2-run case with the older run under, no history longer than 2 runs and no job missing or under now
the trend warning is matched bare, the JSON line is parsed in one case only, and the failed-job check asserts only the exit
a job over the limit is only a plain log line: no annotation on any run, so a PR that slows CI shows nothing
the JSON line names no run, attempt, commit or event, and leaves out failed jobs and their times
the Windows parts list and the slice count in the run line are separate literals, so a part dropped leaves tests unrun with CI green
the project template comment names a lane-state trend that nothing feeds
a failed fetch of the earlier main runs turns main's required check red for a report-only trend
3 in a row misses a job over on 2 of every 3 main runs, and growth below the limit has no signal
each Windows leg is judged alone, so the Windows suite can grow to about 360 s in all with no line
a re-run of an older main run reads later main runs as its history
a renamed job or a shard that moves matrix index starts its trend afresh
without --plan the Windows split packs by order, so part 0 carries most one-test files
with the 30 s cap on Windows a known 40 s hook test prints an over-cap line every run
a stderr check in the 180 s budget test is now always true
no test holds ci.yml passing --history on a main push
